gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI Elite 400's single solar input is limited to 12–60 V and 20 A, so its 2× 350 W kit (33 V open-circuit per panel) cannot be wired in series (66 V) and in parallel tops out below 660 W of its 700 W rating.
standout_why: Compared against the two cited StormWatts pages (240 V solar-input comparison; bundle vs buying separately), the cited PowerSized DELTA Pro 3 review and StormWatts' uncited same-panel-watts kit page. The solar-input comparison gives voltage and current windows only for the Explorer 5000 Plus, SOLIX S5000, DELTA Pro 3 and F3800 Plus. The bundle page gives only watt caps and does not mention the Elite 400 or R3500. PowerSized gives only '2,600W solar input'. The same-panel-watts page does the same series/parallel check for the Elite 200 V2 (12–60 V, 20 A, two SP200L) and the HomePower 3600 Plus, so the method is not new, but it does not cover the Elite 400, the 350 W panel or any 3,840 Wh kit.
decides: Among the four Elite 400 kits in the size range, the input window decides which panel sets the station can fully use. The 2× 200 W kit fits in series (49.2 V, 10.8 A) and the single 350 W kit fits, so their rated-output refill figures hold as arithmetic. The 2× 350 W kit ($2,325.60 link price) cannot deliver its 700 W into a 20 A input, so its refill column should use the under-660 W ceiling (more than 5.8 h, not 5.5 h) and it should not be named the fastest-refill option for the money. No Elite 400 kit can ever exceed 1,000 W of solar (3.84 h at best), whereas StormWatts lists the DELTA Pro 3 at 2,600 W across two inputs and ALLPOWERS states 2,000 W for the R3500. This does not change the ship-now rule: every Elite 400 kit is a pre-order, and the Elite 400 page today says mid-January for orders placed on or after Nov. 18.

findings.label: Solar input window (maker's words)
findings.note: One solar spec line on the page; no second or high-voltage PV input is listed. The same line appears on the Elite 400 + 2×350 W and + 500 W kit pages. Capacity 3,840 Wh and AC 2,600 W on the same page.

findings.product: BLUETTI 350W Solar Panel (the panel in the Elite 400 + 350 W and + 2× 350 W kits)
findings.label: Open-circuit voltage and supplied cable
findings.value: 33 V Voc; MC4 connectors; box includes one '20A MC4 to XT60 Solar Charging Cable (1.5m)'
findings.note: Page text: 'industry-standard MC4 connectors and a 33V open-circuit voltage (Voc)'. The page lists the Elite 400 as compatible. Its Tech Specs section is empty, so no Isc, Vmp or Imp. Identified as the kit panel by price: $1,499 station + $649 panel = $2,148, which is $299 over the $1,849 kit, matching the kit table's 'vs parts' figure.

findings.label: Series wiring vs the 60 V limit
findings.value: 2 × 33 V = 66 V open-circuit, above the 12–60 V input range
findings.note: Arithmetic from the two maker figures above (Voc at standard test conditions; cold raises it further). The two panels therefore have to be wired in parallel. The kit page gives no wiring instruction and does not list the panel model or cables. Store price $2,448.00 read the same day via storecheck.

findings.label: Most solar power the station can take from this kit in parallel
findings.value: under 660 W of the 700 W rated (20 A × 33 V = 660 W upper bound)
findings.note: Arithmetic: power = current × voltage; current is capped at 20 A and a panel's working voltage is always below its 33 V open-circuit voltage, so the real ceiling is lower than 660 W. Refill arithmetic: 3,840 Wh / 700 W = 5.5 h at rated output, 3,840 / 660 = 5.8 h at the bound. Dealectric has not tested this.

findings.label: Single 350 W panel vs the input window
findings.value: 33 V Voc is inside 12–60 V; 350 W needs at least 10.6 A at 33 V, under the 20 A cap
findings.note: Arithmetic: 350 / 33 = 10.6 A is a lower bound; the working current is higher because the working voltage is below Voc, but still well under 20 A. Refill at rated output: 3,840 / 350 = 11.0 h.

findings.product: BLUETTI 200W Portable Solar Panel (SP200L, the panel in the Elite 400 + 2× 200 W kit)
findings.label: Open-circuit voltage and short-circuit current
findings.note: Identified as the kit panel by price: $1,499 + 2 × $399 = $2,297, which is $398 over the $1,899 kit, matching the kit table. The page's compatibility list names the Elite 200 V2 and Elite 300; the fetch did not show the Elite 400 in it.

findings.label: Series vs parallel on the 12–60 V, 20 A input
findings.value: Series: 49.2 V, 10.8 A (fits). Parallel: 24.6 V, 21.6 A short-circuit (over 20 A)
findings.note: Arithmetic from the SP200L figures and the Elite 400 input line; the kit URL was read via storecheck search only ($1,899.00). Series is the layout that fits both limits, so the full 400 W can reach the station. Refill at rated output: 3,840 / 400 = 9.6 h.

findings.label: Fastest possible solar refill at the input cap
findings.note: Arithmetic at the stated 1,000 W cap; real output is lower. Reaching 1,000 W at 20 A needs an array working at 50 V or more, which leaves little room under the 60 V ceiling.

findings.label: Dispatch text on the store page today
findings.value: "expected to ship in mid-January for orders placed on or after Nov. 18"; a second banner says "Elite 400 ships from mid-December"
findings.note: The two banners conflict on the same page, and the same text appears on the + 2×350 W and + 500 W kit pages. Today is Nov. 18, so the mid-January line applies to an order placed now.

findings.label: Reviewer check of the solar spec
findings.value: 1,000 W max, 12 to 60 V, 20 A max; combined AC + solar up to 2,800 W
findings.note: Dylan Bryan repeats the rated figures and says actual solar input 'depends on the panel configuration, sunlight, temperature, and other conditions'. The review reports no measured solar wattage and no panel wiring.

findings.label: Solar charge ceiling (maker's words)
findings.value: "Maximum 2000W solar charge in 2.5 hours"; 3,168 Wh; 3,200 W inverter
findings.source_title: ALLPOWERS R3500 Home Backup Power Station | 3200W 3168Wh
findings.note: Read from the store's product record via storecheck search (station $1,199.00; SP037 kit $1,803.10; SP039 kit $1,993.10). The product page itself returned HTTP 429 to WebFetch, so the voltage and current window was not read. 3,168 Wh is 20.8% under 4,000 Wh, at the edge of the size line.

findings.label: Solar inputs as StormWatts quotes them
findings.value: High-PV 30–150 V, 15 A, 1,600 W max; Low-PV 11–60 V, 20 A, 1,000 W max; 2,600 W total
findings.source_title: 5 kWh-Class Solar Generators Compared on Solar Input (StormWatts, 2026-11-16)
findings.note: StormWatts' figures, not read on EcoFlow's page by this angle. Shown for contrast: a second, 150 V input is what lets panels be strung in series, which the Elite 400 does not have. PowerSized reported the DELTA Pro 3 solar kits out of stock at EcoFlow on 2026-11-17 (https://powersized.com/reviews/ecoflow-delta-pro-3/).

findings.label: Solar inputs as StormWatts lists them
findings.value: 2 × DC8020 ports, 16–60 V, 12 A each, 1,000 W combined; SolarSaga 500 X 'parallel only, never in series'
findings.source_title: Solar Generator Kits Compared at the Same Panel Watts (StormWatts, 2026-11-08)
findings.note: StormWatts' figures, not read on Jackery's page by this angle. Same 60 V ceiling and 1,000 W cap as the Elite 400, but split across two 12 A ports.
